Flos Puerariae-Semen Hoveniae herb pair ameliorates acute alcohol-induced liver 
injury by dual-modulating IL-11-driven inflammation and restoring lipid 
homeostasis via the PI3K/AKT/mTO pathway.

Li S(1), Wang P(1), Xu Y(1), Shang Y(1), Zhao S(1), Yu C(1), Yu J(1), Chi M(2), 
Han F(3).

ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The flowers of Pueraria Lobata (Willd.) Ohwi and 
Semen Hoveniae (FS) herb pair is a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) 
formulation long utilized for alleviating alcohol intoxication, relieving 
hangovers, and protecting the liver. Although it has been widely applied in 
clinical practice to treat alcoholic liver disease (ALD), the mechanisms 
underlying its multi-target efficacy, particularly its active absorbed 
constituents and their impact on lipid metabolism and inflammatory pathways, 
warrant further investigation.
AIM OF THE STUDY: To elucidate the active material basis and multi-target 
mechanisms of FS herb pair against acute alcohol-induced liver injury (AALI) by 
integrating serum pharmacochemistry, network pharmacology, lipidomics, and in 
vivo experimental validation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Bioactive components absorbed in rat serum following oral 
administration were identified using HPLC-FT-ICR MS. Potential therapeutic 
targets were computationally predicted and their possible binding interactions 
were assessed via molecular docking. In vivo, a mouse model of AALI was 
established and treated with the FS herb pair. Hepatoprotective effects were 
evaluated through histopathology, biochemical assays, oxidative stress 
indicators, and inflammatory cytokine profiling. Serum lipid profiles were 
analyzed using UPLC-QE-Orbitrap-MS-based lipidomics, and key signaling proteins 
(PI3K, AKT, mTOR, CYP2E1) and IL-11 expression were assessed by Western blotting 
and immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: A total of 20 F S herb pair-derived prototype components were 
identified in rat serum. Integrated analysis prioritized potential interactions 
between these constituents and targets such as AKT1, TNF, and EGFR, which were 
supported by favorable computationally predicted docking scores. In vivo 
validation demonstrated that FS herb pair significantly ameliorated 
alcohol-induced hepatic histopathological damage, reduced ALT, AST, and lipid 
accumulation (TC, TG). Mechanistically, FS herb pair suppressed CYP2E1-mediated 
oxidative stress (ROS, MDA) and downregulated the pro-inflammatory IL-11 
signaling axis. Lipidomic analysis identified 44 lipid biomarkers, revealing 
that FS herb pair restored glycerophospholipid and fatty acid metabolism 
homeostasis. Alcohol exposure suppressed PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, and FS herb 
pair treatment partially restored this pathway. The observation that LY294002 
attenuated the protective effects of FS herb pair provides pharmacological 
evidence consistent with a role for PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation in FS-mediated 
hepatoprotection.
CONCLUSION: The traditional FS herb pair alleviates AALI through a 
multi-dimensional mechanism. It dually mitigates CYP2E1/ROS-driven oxidative 
stress and IL-11-mediated inflammation, while restoring lipid homeostasis 
associated with the activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. This study provides 
supporting preclinical evidence for the traditional use of FS herb pair in AALI 
management.
